title: Wager atomicity is a compensating saga, not one transaction
observed: Buy-ins are debited seat by seat. A failure refunds already-applied debits and records refund-failed evidence. Table cashouts pay seat by seat and roll back on failure. The escrow record is written only after the loop, so a reload or crash mid-loop leaves debits without an escrow record (recoverable only from TransactionEngine audit entries carrying the escrowId). Failure handling is careful and tested (G22), but this is not the 'whole trade fails' atomicity OSI asks for.
intendedOwnership: TransactionEngine (OSI: atomic where possible).
proposedSolution: Owner decides whether compensating sagas satisfy 'atomic where possible'. If not, add a TransactionEngine multi-actor adjustment (all deltas validated, applied and verified as one operation), shared with Holonet payouts (F-HOL-002). At minimum, persist an 'escrowing' state with the escrowId before the first debit.
regressionTests: tests/ti4c0-g22-wager-refund-replay.test.mjs, plus an interrupted-escrow test.
foundryAcceptance: Reload the GM client during escrow; inspect the ledger.
simplificationBenefit: One multi-party credit primitive across Holonet and games.

intendedOwnership: Undecided: OSI says TransactionEngine is the single source of truth with no parallel ledgers, while V-P6C-19 approves a Party Fund workflow with its own ledger entry.
proposedSolution: Owner decides whether the Party Fund becomes a TransactionEngine-managed account (one ledger, atomic with actor deltas) or is a documented A-10 exception. Until then, no new Party Fund writers.

regressionTests: tests/ti4c0-g26-party-fund-integrity.test.mjs
foundryAcceptance: Party Fund contribute/charge/payout plus vehicle ammo purchase.

title: Trade/payout rollback is a parallel atomicity engine using whole-actor overwrite and item delete-and-recreate
observed: When a multi-actor trade or job payout fails, Holonet restores each actor from a pre-operation toObject snapshot. Effects get the same treatment. Results: (a) item and effect ids are expected to change, breaking id references such as equipped slots or upgrade links (Foundry default behavior, FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED); (b) any concurrent change to those actors (HP, conditions, other transactions) is silently reverted; (c) restore success is not verified (CR-HOL-02). This duplicates the exact-snapshot transactional rollback already in ActorEngine.applyMutationPlan / TransactionEngine (TI4-C0 G06-S1). Only the rollback path is affected; the success path is not.
intendedOwnership: OSI / A-10: TransactionEngine owns atomic trades (credits, item transfer, approval, rollback).
proposedSolution: Owner decision. (a) Move multi-actor trade/payout settlement into a TransactionEngine operation (e.g. extend executeMutationTransaction to multi-actor plans) that uses targeted inverse operations and exact verification. (b) Minimum fix: restore only the fields and items the operation touched, use keepId:true, and verify the result.
alternatives: Keep the current behavior and document it as a known L3 limitation (not recommended).
regressionTests: Test: forced failure mid-trade; assert item ids unchanged and unrelated actor fields untouched after rollback.
foundryAcceptance: Force a counter-offer failure between two owned actors; inspect item ids and equipped state.
risk: High; credit movement and item identity.

proposedSolution: Add an escrow-level invariant check that refuses or routes to GM approval when the sum exceeds the pot. Instrument it first to confirm whether it is ever violated.
regressionTests: Unit test with balances exceeding the pot.
